items.text:
@david__booth Oh yeah well mine…   :) 

1. Gave a solo founder an engineering team's throughput. A full audit of the core repo overnight: 230 items swept, real defects classified, and 12 fixes shipped as review-ready PRs by morning - each with reproducible test evidence. One was a persistence bug silently failing on every write for two weeks - the kind of thing that kills a pilot in week one.

2. Runs the product's own development on the product's standard. The repair-verification harness is now a required check on every change. When CI failed, the failure got reproduced locally and root-caused to a dependency-pinning gap - fixed and green inside 24 hours, with a spec deviation (a loose test-count assertion) caught before review. No "works on my machine," ever.

3. Fact-checks the company before the market does. A weekly review that separates fact from inference caught that six "merged" PRs in the internal record were actually closed unmerged, and killed an inflated test-coverage claim before it could reach external copy. A diligence team would have found these. They won't.

4. Treated the first external proof like a launch review. The flagship demonstration - Apex finding and verifiably fixing a real defect in widely-used open-source software - got a full go/no-go preflight: target pinned and verified, repair scope capped (4 files, 400 lines, 1 repair, 2 attempts, zero merge authority), and an honest list of what's still owed before the run happens. Proof first, claims second.

5. Built the category narrative engine. A research-blog GTM - "let the ideas and evidence do the selling": four posts drafted under strict rules (only what the product provably does today, answer-first, framed in money and risk), plus an evidence-grounded AI terminal on the homepage that answers questions about Apex from its actual records. The site stays deliberately gated until the external proof is public - the blog will open on evidence, not vapor. Alongside that, a 50-account verified X network targeting the exact category: the verification and governance layer for AI-written software.

Thats just in the last 3 days

EA Sports UFC 5 Game Update

Ahead of UFC 322, EA SPORTS UFC 5 is dropping an exciting new content update celebrating some of the sport’s most action-packed fighters and introducing a rising contender looking to showcase his dominance in the Octagon.

One of the most feared welterweights in UFC history, “Ruthless” Robbie Lawler, makes his return to UFC 5 with his UFC 40 Alter Ego. The UFC Hall-of-Famer first made waves with a quick victory over Tiki Ghosn, showcasing the relentless striking that would define his career. Fans can now step into the Octagon and experience Lawler’s legendary ferocity for themselves with this all-new throwback Alter Ego.

Dan Hooker also joins the latest update, bringing his all-action style to UFC 5. The Hangman’s UFC 305 bout against Mateusz Gamrot saw him in a back-and-forth battle, ending in a split-decision victory and Fight of the Night honors. This iconic moment in Hooker’s career cemented his status as a fearless and versatile fighter, and can now be relived through his UFC 305 Alter Ego.

Middleweight legend Dan Henderson is up next, returning with his UFC 100 Alter Ego. Henderson delivered one of MMA’s most unforgettable highlight-reel moments, landing the iconic H-Bomb on rival Michael Bisping. Even amidst the chaos, Hendo’s precision and power reminded fans why he’s considered one of the sport’s all-time greats.

One of the true GOATs of MMA, Amanda Nunes, rounds out the collection with her UFC 232 Alter Ego – spotlighting her legendary title fight against Cris Cyborg, where The Lioness became the first woman to defeat Cyborg in the Octagon with a stunning first-round knockout. The victory solidified her legacy as one of the most dominant fighters in MMA history and also highlighted her precise striking and devastating power. Fans can now step into the Octagon as the featherweight icon and recreate one of the most historic moments in women’s MMA.

Rounding out the update, rising middleweight Roman Kopylov makes his UFC 5 debut ahead of his matchup against Gregory Rodrigues at UFC 322. Kopylov is looking to prove himself in one of MMA’s most competitive divisions and reenter the rankings to continue climbing the ladder.

Whether you’re a long-time fan or new to the sport, the latest UFC 5 update offers something for everyone. Fire up EA SPORTS UFC 5 now to see these incredible fighters in action! (Credit: UFC: PR)

Fallout Season 2 Sets Weekly Release Schedule on Prime Video

The schedule begins with Episode 1 on December 17 at 12 a.m. PT, followed by weekly Wednesday drops through the February 4 finale. This moves away from Season 1's full binge release in 2024, matching the style of shows like The Boys. Fans appreciate the drawn-out excitement and holiday timing, though some prefer the old format or later East Coast slots. Production has wrapped, and the trailer is out for the post-apocalyptic series based on Bethesda games.

News

Shōgun and Fallout director joins Amazon's God of War adaptation

Emmy-winning director Frederick E.O. Toye will contribute to Amazon's God of War adaptation.

As Deadline reports, Toye will reportedly direct the first two episodes. He is known for his work on other Amazon series including Fallout, The Boys and The Terminal List.

Toye won an Emmy for his work on the FX historical drama series Shōgun, of which he directed four episodes.

The director also worked on episodes of Lost, American Gods, The Walking Dead, Watchmen, Westworld, and Snowpiercer.

Toye joins showrunner Ronald D. Moore, who also serves as writer and executive producer.

Moore joined the team last October following the departure of original showrunner Rafe Judkins alongside producers Hawk Ostby and Mark Fergus.

Pre-production of Amazon's God of War adaptation is currently underway in Vancouver, and is set to air for two seasons.

It will be co-produced by Sony Pictures Television and Amazon MGM Studios alongside PlayStation Productions and Moore's Tall Ship Productions.

Sony Pictures Entertainment initially announced Amazon's God of War series in 2022 in tandem with a Gran Turismo film produced by Columbia Pictures and a Horizon series on Netflix.

The Gran Turismo film released in 2023, while the Horizon series was reportedly cancelled following a Rolling Stone report that accused its showrunner of "toxic, bullying, manipulative, and retaliatory behaviour."

Earlier this year, Sony announced that the Horizon project would now be a film, and will be produced by Columbia Pictures in partnership with PlayStation Productions.

A Helldivers 2 adaptation was also announced alongside the Horizon movie. The Hollywood Reporter recently announced that Fast and Furious director Justin Lin will direct the movie.

Lin will also produce the adaptation, with screenwriter Gary Dauberman (It, Annabelle) on board to pen the script. (Deadline, GB, X and AI News)

items.text:
Got one advice for your AI launch videos 

Slow tf down it’s like a kid with adhd made them, can’t even keep up 🥲

Sources 👇

• NVIDIA newsroom (28/09): Open Agent Safety Platform
  https://t.co/d882oMzaBX
• GlobeNewswire same day:
  https://t.co/xvoQSnSBUd
• NVIDIA tech blog — OpenShell 0.1.0:
  https://t.co/522CWN8A2K
• GitHub (Apache-2.0, ~8.9k★): https://t.co/N5i99zQ7r5
• Docs: https://t.co/7GaWQbhVvP
• Works with: Claude Code · Codex · Pi · Hermes (+ more)

OpenShell agent-safety checklist for vibe coders 🔒

1. Deny-by-default egress — allowlist hosts, not “the internet”
2. L7 inspect HTTP/GraphQL/MCP — read-only ≠ write on the same API
3. DNS is part of the policy surface (yesterday’s lesson)
4. Keep real credentials OUTSIDE the sandbox (provider injection)
5. Placeholder keys must fail if sent to the wrong host
6. Landlock filesystem: agent can’t roam home/.ssh/.env
7. Seccomp / process: no privilege escalation, no fork bombs
8. Separate Gateway / Supervisor / Sandbox — never one blob
9. Hot-reload network policy; recreate sandbox for FS/process changes
10. Policy Advisor drafts changes — human approves (agent can’t self-approve)
11. Formal policy prover before you widen access
12. Audit trail (OCSF) on every allow/deny
13. Scope binaries (curl vs claude vs node) per endpoint
14. MCP servers get the same allowlist as REST
15. Multi-tenant workspaces: team A can’t see team B’s providers
16. Red-team: “what boring path still talks outside?”
17. After a deny storm: don’t auto-widen — shrink the task
18. Docker/K8s drivers for local → shared infra without rewriting the agent
19. Pair with Claude Managed Agents / BlueField when you go enterprise
20. Before shipping: prove the policy, don’t narrate it

Sandbox escape → pause training was yesterday.
Runtime that actually enforces policy is today.

items.text: Great insights as always. The funny Achilles heel in all of this with AI, is not talked really about ROI. Mirrors in my QLD lessons, when I/We built the $250Million Green Data Centre "Polaris" in QLD the risk I had then (2009) is worse today in 2026 in the USA is the ROI of the data centres element, now as well as AI itself, different to the China exposure. A real handball smash one might say (perhaps) 😂. I forecast once Trump is out of office, the tech supported industry he has helped, and lack of DC ROI will see the USA AI bubble crash in 2029-2030 due to the DC dilemma (on so many levels) showing signs in late 2028, prior to the USA election. China wins for different reasons.  FYI some environment elements in the 2009 Polaris DC used guideline elements set out in 1976 California by Jerry Brown on the 1st DCs  (addressing noise, water, power) only now being looked at again 50 years later in the USA.. Me testing AI today, reminds me when I did a phone launch for a Chinese company at a global launch in Germany, and had to point out an obvious flaw to me, that they missed (and they were paying me) so delicate. the CEO when it filtered up to him his response was like  .. 灯下黑 .. (if that is right) .. “dark under the lamp.” It was later explained to me. ..  comes from old oil lamps and candles: the light shines outward, but the area right under the lamp itself stays in shadow meaning, people often fail to notice what is closest to them — the obvious thing sitting right in front of their face. I was given a tip of a $2000 phone I could never use in Australia lolz 🤣 - a very nice gesture I still have the phone as a reminder ..
